region: Savorgnano del Torre · Friuli Colli Orientali, Italy
about: Marco Sara farms eight hectares in Savorgnano del Torre, a hamlet of Povoletto in the far northwest of the Friuli Colli Orientali, where vineyards sit in clearings of dense forest beneath the Julian Alps. He and his wife Sandra took over the family estate in 2000, released their first commercial wines in 2003, and still make only about 25,000 bottles a year. Savorgnano is not an official subzone, but locals treat it as one: it is the coolest, wettest corner of the appellation, with up to 1,800 mm of rain a year.

The estate is certified organic. Savorgnano’s hillsides are rich in ponca, the crumbly, calcium-rich marl layered with sandstone that Slovenians call opoka, and the best of these slopes were traditionally kept for white grapes. Ribolla Gialla, Friuli’s ancient native white, is pressed directly with no skin contact, fermented without malolactic conversion and rested six to eight months on its lees before bottling. Sara is openly sceptical of skin-macerated, deliberately funky whites; his aim is a clean wine through which the place, not the winemaking, does the talking.

In the glass the house style is fresh and light-footed: Italian tasting notes for recent vintages describe acacia blossom, aromatic herbs, anise and elderflower over a soft, clean palate with gentle acidity, the kind of white Friulians drink at the table every day. It is a wine for the table rather than the cellar: Sara calls his Ribolla a territorial, everyday white, and its lightness and lift make it an easy partner for vegetables, shellfish and simply cooked fish.
